newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER - INTERNAZIONALE DRAWN AGAINST BOAVISTA IN UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - INTERNAZIONALE DRAWN AGAINST BOAVISTA IN UEFA CUP.

text.p: UEFA Cup specialists Internazionale, who needed a penalty shoot-out to see off the challenge of Casino Graz in the second round, were drawn against Portuguese side Boavista in Friday's third round draw.
Inter were taken to the limit by the unfancied Austrian side on Tuesday after having England midfielder Paul Ince sent off in extra time.

Boavista are not regarded as one of the heavyweights of the competition but Inter, bidding for a third UEFA Cup triumph in seven seasons, will not treat them lightly in view of their close shave against Casino Graz.
Spain's Valencia, conquerors of holders Bayern Munich in the first round, were paired with Turkey's Besiktas, conquerors of Legia Warsaw in the second round.

Valencia will be without goalkeeper Andoni Zubizaretta for the home leg. He will be serving an automatic suspension for his sending-off in the the second half of Tuesday's goalless draw with Slavia Prague.
The Spanish side qualified 1-0 on aggregate.
The three German clubs to reach the last 16 managed to avoid each other in Friday's draw.
Hamburg face arguably the sternest test after being paired with Monaco, surprise conquerors of Germany's Borussia Moenchengladbach in the last round.
Karlsruhe meet Denmark's Brondby while Schalke take on Belgians Club Brugge.
The clash between English premier league big spenders Newcastle and French side Metz could be one of the best of the round.

Both were impressive winners in their second round ties, Newcastle thumping Hungary's Ferencvaros 4-0 in the second leg on Tuesday for a 6-3 aggregate triumph and Metz ousting Sporting Lisbon 3-2 on aggregate.
